title: Opposition watch: what Democrats plan for RFK Jr. and MAHA
context: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate on Nov 3, 2026, with Alaska and Mississippi Senate races and dozens of House races still uncalled as of Nov 4. The new Congress convenes Jan 3, 2027; until then Republicans hold the gavels.
method: Daily news sweep. Each item records who, what, and its status: 'stated intent' (a pledge, interview or plan), 'on file' (letter, bill or resolution already filed), 'scheduled' (hearing, markup or vote on a calendar), 'in court', 'done' (enacted or held), or 'reported' (press framing and personnel facts, not a Democratic action). Pledges are not actions; status changes only when a primary record (committee site, congress.gov, docket) shows it.

items.actor: House Oversight — Robert Garcia (then ranking member) to HHS
items.summary: Request 3 seeks 'All communications between HHS or CDC employees and the Children’s Defense Fund, Aaron Siri, and any other individual or organization with whom HHS has consulted on vaccines.' Request 7 covers ACIP-member messages 'on official and personal devices'; Request 9 seeks conflict documentation for 'all external parties who presented or contributed to the ACIP meeting.' Sent from the minority; can be reissued as a majority subpoena after Jan 3.
items.watch: A reissued or corrected request (e.g., 'Children’s Health Defense'), and the first letters sent directly to outside groups.

items.summary: Names Children’s Health Defense, Lyn Redwood, Aaron Siri, David Geier, Stefanie Spear, Calley Means/Truemed and Finn Kennedy’s investment fund as conflicts or influences; it is the likely roadmap for majority document requests.
items.watch: Named parties receiving direct requests; GreenMedInfo and Stand for Health Freedom are not named in it.

items.actor: House Oversight — Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA), expected chair
items.summary: Garcia plans probes of Kennedy's vaccine-policy changes, including the ACIP purge and schedule revisions. Democrats suspect 'conservative, anti-vax interest groups' are driving those decisions and are likely to subpoena communications between those groups and the administration. Garcia posted 'LAWYER UP' on election night.
items.watch: Outside MAHA and medical-freedom groups that corresponded with HHS should expect document requests; preservation obligations attach once requests arrive.

items.actor: House Energy and Commerce — Rep. Frank Pallone (D-NJ), likely chair; Rep. Diana DeGette
items.summary: Pallone and DeGette demanded CDC's scientific assessments and drafts behind the new childhood schedule (Jan 14, 2026). Pallone and Sanders opened an investigation of FDA's fast-track program (Nov 24, 2025). These requests can be renewed as majority letters and, if authorized, subpoenas.
items.watch: Majority staff typically re-send minority-era requests in January with deadlines.

items.actor: Senate HELP — Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT), expected chair
items.summary: Sanders and all HELP Democrats demanded Kennedy testify (Dec 2025 letter) and Sanders suggested calling ousted CDC director Susan Monarez. Kennedy committed at confirmation to testify quarterly on the chair's request, which Sanders would now control.
items.watch: First HELP oversight hearing with Kennedy; a Monarez appearance.

items.actor: Senate Finance — Sen. Ron Wyden (D-OR), expected chair
items.summary: Wyden summarized his midterm reaction in one word: 'Subpoenas.' Finance has jurisdiction over HHS nominations, Medicare and Medicaid.
items.watch: Nomination leverage over HHS sub-agency picks.

items.actor: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI); Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-MI)
items.summary: Stevens filed an article of impeachment against Kennedy citing research cuts, the firing of all 17 ACIP members and COVID-vaccine access limits. Thanedar has a separate resolution. Both stalled under GOP control; a Democratic House could move them, though removal needs two-thirds of the Senate.
items.watch: Any Judiciary Committee referral or a privileged floor resolution after Jan 3.

items.summary: Andrews, a pediatrician, campaigned on 'impeach and remove RFK Jr.' 314 Action says questioning Kennedy under oath was one of the most motivating factors for its candidates.
items.watch: Whether the incoming doctor caucus forms a bloc on HELP or Finance.

items.summary: 'First 100 Hours' goals include guaranteed no-cost coverage of recommended vaccines regardless of federal recommendation changes and restoring withheld NIH funding. Listed 100-day bills would codify ACIP practices to require 'best available, peer-reviewed scientific evidence' and bar political appointees from reviewing NIH grants.
items.watch: Bill text and numbers in January; Trump veto and the 60-vote Senate filibuster limit what becomes law.

items.actor: 15 Democrat-led states (14 AGs + Pennsylvania governor); AAP and IDSA
items.summary: The states sued to rescind the new childhood schedule and vacate the reconstituted ACIP. A separate AAP/IDSA suit already won stays on the new ACIP appointments and schedule changes; the government is appealing.
items.watch: Appeal rulings; incoming Democratic governors (Iowa, Ohio, Georgia, Texas) joining the suit.

items.actor: House Democrats' 'Reclaiming MAHA' memo; Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez; Center for American Progress
items.summary: The working-group agenda includes 'Reclaiming MAHA and Protecting American Families,' recommending removal of Trump-administration protections for glyphosate. Ocasio-Cortez has spent months courting MAHA advocates. CAP released a food-and-chemicals plan with polling that 37% of Trump voters are open to a Democrat running on core MAHA issues.
items.watch: Split strategy: attack Kennedy on vaccines while adopting the food/pesticide agenda. Recommendations, not an adopted caucus platform.

items.actor: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-MI); Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ); Moms Across America
items.summary: El-Sayed's 'Building a Healthier America' plan calls for banning certain pesticides; Booker backs pesticide-liability legislation. Moms Across America endorsed Ocasio-Cortez, Booker, Pappas, Merkley, Pingree and Davids for opposing farm-bill pesticide shields.
items.watch: Pesticide-liability and food bills where MAHA priorities and Democratic sponsors overlap.

items.summary: Coverage frames election night as a MAHA defeat: Kennedy-backed Zach Lahn lost the Iowa governor race in a landslide, MAHA Caucus chair Sen. Roger Marshall lost in Kansas, and Kennedy-backed Joe Mitchell lost IA House. STAT says MAHA 'factored little into key races.'
items.watch: Test this framing against the War Room's pre-registered overlay before conceding or rebutting it.

items.summary: Marshall had aimed to chair HELP in a Republican Senate; his loss and the flip hand the gavel to Sanders. Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who has raised concerns about Kennedy, could become the top Republican on HELP.
items.watch: Ranking-member pick; whether any Republican joins oversight requests.

calendar.what: 120th Congress convenes; Democrats take the committee gavels

log.note: First sweep after the midterms. Added primary records behind the outside-group subpoena threat.
